Major Despodov did not want to open fire upon the above mentioned targets without orders, requested approval from the superiors." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then it says: "Around 1800 to 1900 hours, first, the person Johan talked with the president of the state and then Major Despodov talked with the president. The president asked him whether he is under the command of General Sokol. Major Despodov answered yes. The president told him, Good. I will talk to the General Sokol, and I will call you again." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then if you look at the following paragraph: After 2200 hours on 11 August 2001." Do you see that, that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It says: "That the above listed persons of the Ministry of Interior came again and demanded orders to start the action and they disassociated themselves from the same while Johan Tarculovski said tomorrow at 4.30 hours I will start the action."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would you mind reading more slowly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: "Major Mitre Despodov also asked for approval an orders for supporting the action of Johan Tarculovski, even though it had been agreed earlier. Johan Tarculovski told Major Despodov there will be orders from the president or from the persons around him." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, this is -- took place -- this conversation took place at 2200 hours on the 11th of August, 2001. And according to this report, there was still no order from Sokol Mitrevski, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Then the report continue and it says that: "On Sunday, 12 August 2001, at 4.30 hours the person Johan Tarculovski with other persons, Ministry of Interior reservists, started the action. Immediately after the start of the action Captain Grozdanovski called up Major Despodov an informed him about the start of the action. And then it continues and it says that they called Major Despodov and requested support for shooting at the mentioned buildings and Major Despodov agreed. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then if you look at the very last paragraph of this report, Mr. Keskovski, it says that around 8.00 --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could have the text raised on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Certainly. Do you see it now? All right.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's fine now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now at the very bottom it says: "Around 0800 hours, Major Despodov called the commander and asked him whether he had received any orders from General Sokol Mitrevski for an action against the village of Ljuboten." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then it says that the commander answered that for the present he had not received any orders and after this he called personally General Sokol Mitrevski who said that he had not issued any orders. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then if we can please turn to the following page. Just if you look at the very first sentence.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps in the Macedonian it might be at the very bottom of the page. No, I'm sorry, Madam Registrar it might be at the bottom of the previous page. I'm looking for the passage that begins with the passage: "Around 8.30 hours." All right. I think it's there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, if we look at the paragraph that begins with around 8.30 hours. It says around 8.30 hours Major Despodov again called the commander and asked him whether the superiors know about the action that is being organised and carried out by the Ministry of Interior in the village of Ljuboten. And the commander answered that General Sokol Mitrevski is not informed about the mentioned action and that he will come personally to positions to resolve the situation. And after that, when the commander saw how -- how the operation was being carried out by the Ministry of Interior, he ordered that actions -- to stop. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So by 8.30 in the morning on the 12th of August, Major Despodov is still asking about whether an order had been issued by his superiors, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you are read to go me now is not a statement of Major Despodov. It is a narration of a certain person who is recounting what had happened there while he was not on the ground. Whether Major Despodov received or not this order, it's a question that should be asked of him. All the rest is conjecture which pertains to this report and it's mainly hearsay, something which a person has heard happen. Therefore, I cannot answer your question. Major Despodov received an order from the president to undertake activities within his competency.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: We see here --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I heard. As for the undersigned, what the undersigned person on this report heard, I don't know. This is a different matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, I appreciate that you don't know, Mr. Keskovski. But this is a report from the assistant to the commander for security in that area in the army, right? And --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But he is recounting something he had heard about while not being present there. This is not the same thing. If I'm telling you about something which I had heard about, then this can be understood in different ways as speculation or tendency to prove something. As far as I'm able to note, he also told him and then he answered. Again, the drafter of this report spoke with persons and on the basis on that conversation he drafted the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, we also see here, Mr. Keskovski, that commander Kapoce [sic] stopped any measures or any action, or any -- of measures of support when he realised that an order from the army superiors had not been issued, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what is written here, whether this is it accurate or not, I wouldn't be able to tell you. I was not present there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to please turn to tab 8 in your binder. And I will be referring to P304. If you can turn to the second page, please, the very first paragraph. This is the report that was referred to earlier in your examination-in-chief that was written by the commander Kopacev. And perhaps for e-court purposes, I will be referring to the second page, please. Thank you. Now, if I can draw your attention, Mr. Keskovski, to the very first paragraph on that page. It says: "After 2200 hours on the same day," and that's referring to 11 August 2001 as we have just seen in the previous report.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but I don't see this on the screen. It says on the 12th of August at 430. This is what I'm looking at. Perhaps it's on the previous page.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I believe it's on page N001-4677 in the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You see it now?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Says that: "After 2200 hours on the same day, the above mentioned persons from the Ministry of Interior led by Johan Tarculovski came from the second time to Mitre Despodov regarding the action. Johan Tarculovski told all of them that the action starts at 430 in the morning --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you for reading slowly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Certainly, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: -- "regardless whether or not there would be army support." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Then it says that Major Despodov told that he has no authority to support the action. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But despite that, Major Despodov undertook all measures in order to implement the action successfully in case it was approved by our side. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to go to tab 42, which is 65 ter 1D00936, please. And I will perhaps be referring to specific pages. And I would ask if Madam Registrar can pull up the Macedonian on the screen and the English. The first page I will be referring to, Madam Registrar, is page 17 in the English and it is 1D00-7925. 17 in the hard copy, I should say. Now, this is an interview carried out by investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor of Sokol Mitrevski. And if we look at page 17, Sokol -- if we look at the previous pages, actually, Sokol Mitrevski is asked about this action in the village of Ljuboten. And if I can perhaps just ask for context, if we can refer to page 15, which is 1D00-7923. And Sokol Mitrevski says: "At the beginning I would like to say" - this is about line 6 of the transcript - "That I have no connection whatsoever with the events of Ljuboten. And I was informed after the events by the commander of the Guardist Brigade. I was informed by Colonel Kopacev who was commander of the Guardist Brigade that had the position above the village of Ljuboten at the time. I requested from the commander personally to submit a report with all information that was ..." and it continues. Then if you look at page 17, Sokol Mitrevski explains at the very top of that page, at line 2: "There was a commanding system in an army. You know, once an army where only one person makes decisions." And there is an indiscernible word there. And then he goes on to say: "Command is planning; the units are performing. And every performance should be preceded by an order. So once again I would like to resume that the army nor the army officials were involved in any way. That was an action by the Ministry of Interior. And he continues. Then he says: "Who said that nobody was supposed to know about this action." This at about line 13 "apart from himself and some people from the ministry. I don't want to justify or find justification for the major because he violated the basic commanding chain; he was punished and he was revoked from his position. Do you see that, Mr. Keskovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it, but only in the English version and I am able to hear what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I appreciate that. Do you suppose, Mr. Keskovski, that Major Despodov would have been disciplined for his actions for violating the chain of command, if he had received a direct order from the president?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not competent to provide an answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Before we continue and perhaps again I'm mindful of Your Honour's instructions of the previous session, but the question was a loaded one if I may say so because it assumed that Major Despodov had indeed been disciplined or punished in any way. The evidence as we have it on the transcript from the major is that he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mettraux. The problem is referring only to an unexhibited interview. The content which of is no weight, unless adopted by the witness, and he cannot. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: May I continue -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Keskovski, Sokol Mitrevski continues and he says: "But as a human being, not as a general, but as a commander of a brigade I assume that he was impressed from the phone call with the president. He thought he was a big shot, you know, speaking with the president. Maybe it was a set-up conversation, I don't know." And he goes on. Isn't General Mitrevski saying here that Major Despodov made certain decisions on his own?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer this question. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa could the Chamber intervene to point out that you are basing this upon a statement which is not in evidence. There is no oral evidence of these matters, and the cross-examination is therefore of no value to the Chamber at all unless the witness is able to say of his own knowledge that these events are correct. And this witness's position is that he cannot speak about these events of his own knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour. I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you, Mr. Keskovski, to please turn to tab 19.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And I will be referring to P379.04. If we can perhaps bring that up in the e-court system. Now, this was information obtained in 2003 by a commission that was set up by the minister, Hari Kostov, to investigate the events in the village of Ljuboten. This is a report that was dated 25 November 2003. And if I can draw your attention to about the fourth paragraph at the -- on the first page of this report, Johan Tarculovski was interviewed by members of the commission and it says: "In this direction, Tarculovski was asked who gave him orders to go to the village Ljuboten and who gave the orders to fire and which persons were present with him in the village of Ljuboten." "In his reply to these question, Tarculovski first explained that at the previous meeting he was summoned as an employee of the ministry, while now he is a civilian because he has resigned from the ministry. He also said that he left for Ljuboten on his own will, and that he did not get orders from anyone to go to the village of Ljuboten." Do you see that.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Then he goes on, very bottom of the paragraph -- of the page. Says: "With regard to the question about the manner about entrustment much weapon, Tarculovski replied that he was called by the minister of internal affairs at that time who told him to determine a reserve force of people who will provide the security of vital state facilities." And it continues. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So even when Johan Tarculovski was asked about this by the commission, he did not say that the president ordered him to go to Ljuboten and undertake an action or provide the president with information, did he?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to answer this?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Find me one place in this statement, in a previous statement, or the statement before that, my statements, where I said that the president ordered Mr. Johan Tarculovski to go to Ljuboten. In all my statements, I indicated the village of Ljubanci and what has Mr. Tarculovski stated, I can't comment on that. This is not my right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And in here it says that Mr. Tarculovski -- Mr. Tarculovski says, at least to the commission, that he was in fact in Ljuboten, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are reading this. This is what Tarculovski has stated. This is a statement that I see for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. I will move on. Now, you've testified, Mr. Keskovski, that Ljube Boskoski is an honest man, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That he wouldn't hide from the truth, would he?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you an answer for this -- to this question. In my opinion, he is an honest person, and I don't believe that he would hide from the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: He wouldn't misrepresent deliberately what happened in 2001, would he?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you answers to questions that you should ask of Mr. Ljube Boskoski and not myself. Ask me, I might give you my opinion. I can't tell what you Mr. Ljube Boskoski is thinking.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, I'd like you to please go to tab 2 of the Prosecution binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And I will be referring to P402, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I will be referring, firstly, to page 32 in the English hard copy, page 66 in your copy, Mr. Keskovski, and in e-court page 35 in the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 35?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, I'm referring to page 66 in the Macedonian hard copy. Now, first of all, this is a --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: This is a book, Mr. Keskovski, that was written by Ljube Boskoski, titled My Battle for Macedonia, regarding the events of 2001. Are you familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Have you read the book?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I skimmed through it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if I can draw to your attention to about the bottom of the page in your copy, where it says, paragraph that begins: "However the tension in Aracinovo was ever more disturbing." Have you found that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, in this paragraph, Mr. Boskoski is talking about the events in Aracinovo in 2001. And he says this: "This village was entered by some 30 armed and uniformed people. And the information from the village confirmed that newcomers had immediately disposed in several locations." And then he continues. And towards the end of the paragraph, about five lines from the bottom he says: "As a result the police in cooperation with the army of the Republic of Macedonia strengthened its security and defence activities. We reinforced the police presence at the entrances and exits of Aracinovo as well as on the vital positions around the village. Our objective was to make use of the operation and technical measures of the security forces to prevent this militant group from leaving Aracinovo," and he continues. Now first of all, isn't he saying in this passage that the police forces were working in cooperation with the army?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, they would cooperate. This is something normal.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So the police forces were not subordinated to the army, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're speaking about this specific action, the police forces were subordinated to the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Isn't what Ljube Boskoski saying -- isn't what Ljube Boskoski saying here is that they were working jointly with the army?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that your question is not proper, because to cooperate means the same. Cooperation is cooperation, so it means that they undertook activities together, and they're not one and the same institution, so that they could be considered as one. They are two institutions but they cooperate and they undertake measures jointly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, if I can move on --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you would like to -- like me it give you a specific answer, Mr. Boskoski is writing precisely that this was done cooperation with the army. I don't see anything here saying who is in command of whom.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Let's continue, Mr. Keskovski, and I would ask to you please look at page 67 in the Macedonian version in your hard copy. We're still at page 35 in e-court. And now it's page 33 in the English hard copy. And if I can just draw your attention to the paragraph that begins with: "Everything was ready to undertake the Macedonian security forces." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: He says: "Everything was ready to undertake the Macedonian security forces decisive actions against the terrorists in Aracinovo. The only thing we were waiting for was the order from the state highest officials and the crisis management coordination body. I did not agree with the indecisive views of this body which were pushing Macedonia into negotiations with the terrorists, something that the great Albanian national chauvinist centres truly wanted. I made up my mind. I resigned my membership,". And he continues. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Then if you go to page -- I think it's the same page in your version, but in the e-court version it should be page 36 and in English it's at the very bottom. And Mr. Boskoski is here talking about continuing to talk about the action in Aracinovo. And he say: "The action of the Macedonian security forces in Aracinovo confirmed that Macedonia was able to cope alone with enemies of whatever sort." And he continues. Did you find that paragraph? It should be on your screen. It's under the subheading: The people's response.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that paragraph. I have here a paragraph starting with everything was ready to start, a decision was awaited, what you had read previously.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I would ask you, then, to please look at the paragraph below that, immediately after that lengthy paragraph that we just looked at.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is in your paragraph, yes. Very well. A new topic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. And he continue -- Minister Boskoski continues and says: "I saw this myself when I gave the flag to the crew and I told them to plant it in the centre of Aracinovo." So he's talking about being there. Now, nowhere in these passages, Mr. Keskovski, does it say anything about the president, does it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you have read, yes, but I'm not the author of the book.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You need to talk to the author of the book, regarding his views and positions, or at least I think so. I'm not a critic so that I can answer about what Mr. Boskoski has written.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if I can ask you to please turn to -- it would be page 35 in the English; Macedonian page 38 to 39 in the e-court..

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can ask Madam Registrar to pull that up, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it starts at the very bottom of your screen, Mr. Keskovski, of page 38. And he says at the very last paragraph: "I assure you there will be no peace with terrorists. We will continue our action and President Trajkovski will negotiate as a president of a state which wants to become a member of the EU." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So Ljube Boskoski didn't agree very much with the president, did he?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer this question. I am not Ljube Boskoski, I'm not the president. I will tell you again, this is a book written by Mr. Boskoski, so I can't comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mr. Keskovski, did you know Minister Boskoski, or Ljube Boskoski, to be a man who was a peace maker?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I answer this question? I can't answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Was he a forgiving person.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is Christian to forgive.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, I don't think you answered my question, Mr. Keskovski. Was Ljube Boskoski a forgiving person?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like to turn to 65 ter 1117.6, please, which is a short video-clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour perhaps we move on and before Your Honour decide they wish or don't wish to watch this video I will simply indicate what this is. This is again another political speech of Mr. Boskoski. I think one of the month of July 2002. In the course of Sunday of the past weekend, our colleagues from the Prosecution sent us a list of material which indicated they intended to use with Mr. Keskovski. We sent an e-mail to the Prosecution in relation to this particular video as well as another video and a third document asking them to specify the purported relevance of that material to this case and in particular to the evidence of Mr. Keskovski. The Prosecution refused to do so, indicating to us that they had no obligation to do so. In a previous e-mail relating to a previous witness they had indicated that this would reveal their strategy, Your Honour. We believe that this particular video has nothing to do with these proceedings, and it has even less to do, Your Honour, in our submission with the evidence of this particular witness. What the Prosecution is attempt to do is to show you a video of Mr. Boskoski making political statement that have nothing to do with these proceedings. We believe that the Prosecution should be asked to state the alleged relevance of that material to the extent that they can satisfy the Chamber of the prima facie relevance of this matter it could be shown, and Your Honour obviously could decide later what to do with it. The last time such a video was shown, Your Honour had expressed some reservations about the relevance of this material, particularly in relation to the time-frame. The reasons for Your Honours acceptance of the material was of subsequent indication by the Prosecution to the effect that the prime minister, I believe and another state official, I cannot remember at this stage, had been present at the time during this particular political meeting, having seen the video there seems to be no such presence at this particular meeting; and we would wish to hear from the Prosecution what the alleged relevance of that material is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Saxon. The witness is being taken by Ms. Issa it is to her that I should--

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Your Honour with this particular witness, clearly, the Defence has put Mr. Boskoski's character into issue. They asked him questions about Mr. Boskoski's character in their examination-in-chief, and in light of that we are entitled to raise or to provide evidence that relate to character.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The video that you're to put to the witness? What is its nature and character?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a speech given by Minister Boskoski regarding -- in Tetovo on the 29th of July, 2002, and in it he refers to the crisis in 2001. He talks about the Macedonians have the strength to handle any type of crisis. There's no forgiving. Those who killed Macedonia's sons and he continues. So it's a speech that reflects his perception and his views about the crisis in 2001 and reflects and has an impact on his character.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber is not minded to hear this video or to have questions put in respect of it, Ms. Issa. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, are you aware of Minister Boskoski's reaction to the incident in Karpalak?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just correct you. My name is Keskovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for correcting my pronunciation of your name. I'll ask the question again. Are you aware of then-Minister Boskoski's reaction to the incident in Karpalak in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to turn to tab 2, P402, within the same ERN range that we were dealing with earlier, page 46, and the Macedonian is page 51. Page 46 in English. If you can just find the paragraph that starts with: "However, 8 August, 2001."

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I look at page 51, as you said for the Macedonian version, and I don't see any such paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, at the very bottom, it should be at the very bottom of the screen. And Madam Registrar right now moving the page down. So if you look at your screen you will see it. And in the English version it at the very bottom of page 46 in the hard copy. And it says: "However 8 August 2001 was the day when we faced the great Albanian impudent obscured and insulting hypocritical arsenal or anti-Macedonian dishonour."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then he continues: "It was the day that I was devastated by the death of ten soldiers from Prilep. I immediately ordered additional restrict the movement in Aracinovo which was extended for one hour from 2100 hours to 0500 hours. We expected that the committers of the unforgivable crime at the place called Karpalak, having blood-stained their arms to the shoulders will shelter in this village where they were going to plan their further bloody actions. The same addition for restrict movement applied to Tetovo." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, are you aware of Minister Boskoski's views regarding the international community's efforts, and the efforts of the Macedonian government to find a peaceful resolution to the crisis?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer this question. I'm not competent to answer it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Are you saying you're not aware?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't answer it. This what is what it means. You're asking me about Mr. Boskoski, what was the reaction of Mr. Boskoski. During the period of time you're talking about, I was head of the security for the president of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Keskovski you also told us that you know Minister Boskoski personally and that he was your best man at your wedding and you were close to him, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Boskoski was the best man at my wedding, a witness at my wedding, on the 18th of May, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Are you suggesting you didn't know him before the 18th of May, 2002?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him. He was the minister of the interior. And his political positions do not correspond to his presence as the witness, as the best man at my wedding. I don't need to know what was the political position of Mr. Boskoski and how was his attitude towards the international community. I believe your question is irrelevant. I am not able to know what was the thinking of Mr. Ljube Boskoski on the 8th of August, 2001. On the 8th of August, 2001 --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I was head of security for the president, and it was near the completion of the Framework Agreement in Ohrid.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Keskovski, I would ask you to please turn to page 41 to 42 in the Macedonian version perhaps it might be simpler if we can just pull that page up on the screen. And it's page 38 in the English hard copy. And it is under the subheading titled: "Provocations continue." There's a paragraph that begins with: "After the reconciling tones and moves of the highest officials of the Macedonian state ..." Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It says: "After the reconciling tones and moves by the highest officials of the Macedonian state for resolving the crisis, the situation did not only fail to calm down but the Albanian terrorists and extremists continued the provocations." And then he continues. Then if you look at the last paragraph that begins with: "Strange things were taking place." It would be at page 42 in the Macedonian version. He says this: "While the activities of Albanian terrorists was escalating, the international community representative were demanding that the Macedonian security forces restrain from armed actions. These ingenious proposals came from the EU and the USA political representatives in the state, Leotard and Pardew when they paid me a visit in my Ministry of Interior cabinet. They openly requested that the Macedonian security forces refrain from opposing the provocations by the Albanian terrorists. The terminology by the two already changed into insurgence. They explained their attitude by claiming that negotiations must continue in order to find a final solution. And he then says: "I responded fiercely pointing to the fact that we had not been sending to the field sacrificial goats into the jaws of the beasts but rather defenders of the territorial integrity and state sovereignty of the Republic of Macedonia," and he continues. And finally if I can just ask you to turn to page 46 of the Macedonian version. If we can just pull that up on the screen, page 41 in the English. And I will be referring to the paragraph that begins with: "I also pointed out that one side truce which was signed with NATO would be observed." Do you see that on your screen, Mr. Keskovski? Yes?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: In the middle of the paragraph he says: "I was pleasantly surprised by the interest of the reporters in the meeting that I had with the special envoys Leotard and Pardew what did you talk about, one reporter asked. They tried to soften my strict attitudes regarding the Macedonian national interests. I felt that the journalists were pleased with me statement." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Keskovski, I'm going to put a few propositions to you, and I would ask you to simply answer yes or no, okay?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can answer this by yes or no, then the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I put it to you, Mr. Keskovski, that there was no order to attack the village of Ljuboten of president because, had there been one, Major Despodov would not have kept asking about the order until the 12th of August. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are your words. You drew them from this. I can't answer this question. How could I answer it?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I put it to you, Mr. Keskovski --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. Was there any order by the president to attack Ljuboten to Major Despodov? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I put it to you, Mr. Keskovski, that the president's primary certain was to facilitate the Ohrid Agreement in the face of a very difficult crisis in 2001 and that he would have done nothing to jeopardise that agreement in the days leading up to the signing of the agreement. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I put it to you, Mr. Keskovski, that Johan Tarculovski was involved in the action in Ljuboten that day. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer these questions by yes or no. This is your assertion. You are saying that you are asserting this and I can't confirm what you are thinking.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. I put it to you --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the questions are very general.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I put it to you Mr. Keskovski that you have demonstrated bias in favour of Ljube Boskoski who is friend of yours and who was your best man at your wedding and that in your evidence you're merely attempting to give evidence in his favour and that's why you have changed your statement on material points. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Issa. We will have the break now and resume. It will be tight, Mr. Mettraux, but we would hope --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Should be able to do it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. We resume at ten minutes past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Keskovski.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall being asked questions by my colleague of the Prosecution about the statement that you have given to the Office of the Prosecutor, and you have been asked to comment about a number of paragraphs in that statement. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall being asked by my colleague whether when doing so, you attempted to be as accurate and truthful as you could, and you answered that you did. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Now tell me this, if you can recall. How long approximately did the interview with the OTP investigator last?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interview lasted from 9.30 in the morning to 1930 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So that would be about ten hours. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And during the course of the interview, was a transcript a verbatim transcript taken of what you and the investigator were saying to each other, or was it the investigator that was writing things down as you went?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigator was taking notes while I was speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it the case that at the end of those ten hours he provided you with what effectively is a summary of the discussion you had with them. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that the statement that was presented to you was only a portion or a summary of the entire conversation you had with him? Would it be fair?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And tell me this as well. Who was asking the questions during the interview? Was it yourself or the investigator?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was answering the questions of the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did he ever give you a list of written questions or was he asking them orally to you, as you went?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you did not receive the written list of his questions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And who was writing down what was said between you and the investigator? Was it you or was it the investigator?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigator was doing this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And who decided what should be included in the statement and why shouldn't? Was it you or the investigator?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And at the end of the interview, this ten-hour interview you had with the investigator, did he gave you a copy of your statement that you were able to take home with you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did they ever come back to you and ask you whether you would be able to give further information or further clarification or additional information about the information you had already given, and when I say "they," I mean the Office of the Prosecutor. Did they ever come back to you to ask for additional information?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After giving the statement, I was informed that if there was need, I would be contacted again. I agreement to this. In February 2007, the OTP called and they said they wanted to speak with me at the end of February. However, they made no further calls or did not contact me further in March or in April 2007 I received the summons to testify on behalf of the Defence which was signed by Ms. Carla Del Ponte. These are all the contacts which I have had.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D1249. And I would kindly ask the usher, if you could give Mr. Keskovski his Defence binder once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski that would be under tab 1 of your binder, and this is the statement that you have given to the OTP. And I would ask the registry to turn to page 8 of the statement that would be 1D00-9966 and ask you to focus on paragraph 34, please. Mr. Keskovski, I will ask you to locate if you can, paragraph 34 of your statement. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall being asked a number of questions by my colleague of the Prosecutor in relation to that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to read it back to you if I may, the first sentence say this is: "In the afternoon, 10th of August, 2001, the president approved the request and asked me to call Johan Tarculovski. Let me ask you this: Was that statement true and accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you stand by it to this day?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Now let's look at the next sentence it says this: "As I called Johan Tarculovski, the president wanted to speak to him, so that I gave him mobile phone. Again, was that statement true and accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you stand by it to this day?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let's look at the next sentence. It says this: "I was present during the conversation and I heard the president asking Johan Tarculovski to call the next day and inform the president about the situation in the village." Was that statement true and accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you stand by it to this day?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when you told the investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor that you were present during the conversation when you heard the president asking Johan Tarculovski to call the next day, which conversation were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring to the conversation between the president and Tarculovski, about his going to Ljubanci and report being what was going on, on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And was that the conversation that took place on the phone or was that the conversation that took place in the office of the president?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the office of the president. Twice the conversation took place, once over the phone and once in the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And was that the meaning that you intended to communicate to the investigator of Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Was that the meaning that you intended to communicate to the investigator of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And just looking at this paragraph, the paragraph in question, does it seem from that paragraph that the investigator had any wish or need to determine where that particular conversation took place? Does it seem that -- from the statement, that he asked you to specify that?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the course of the interview, I was asked very general questions. For example what do you know by the 10th of August, what do you know about the 11th, 12th of August without any specification or request for specification for any concrete situation. I was not asked about any specific events of this nature which you and the Prosecutor were asking me about.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would it be correct that when there was a need for specification the Prosecutor would ask you a subsequent question, is that the way it worked?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he should have asked me concretely about some things which should have been of interest to him. Which might have been of interest to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now Mr. Mettraux I must interrupt. Ms. Issa has a concern.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour I believe in my submission I believe that during the critical questions regarding the reliability of the statement Mr. Mettraux should not be permitted to lead to ask leading questions of this nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. They have tended to be leading and their probative weight is affected by that. Ms. Issa, you will realise that I have not allowed you to interrupt at a critical point just as I had not allowed Mr. Mettraux to interrupt your cross-examination at those points.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, can I ask you now to look at paragraph 32 of your statement, it's just above. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall being asked a number of questions about this paragraph by my colleague of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would like to read out to you this paragraph or at least the relevant part of it, it says this: "On 10th August 2001 we came back from Ohrid sometimes in the morning and the chief of General Staff of the ARM General Metodija Stamboliski called me by phone and informed me about Ljubotenski Bacila mine incident. Was that statement true and accurate, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you stand by it to this day?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The next sentence reads as follows: "Later on I have passed the information to the president." Same question: Was that statement true and accurate to the best of your knowledge, at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say: "I understood that in mine incident some soldiers of the army got killed and they were from Ljubanci village." Was that statement true and accurate, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you stand by it to this day?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Now, were you asked by the investigator of the Prosecution whether the president had given an order to General Stamboliski, as far as can you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not asked this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And just looking at that paragraph, in particular the section that I have read out to you, does it appear that the investigator had any interest in obtaining any detail from you about what was said between the president, Mr. Stambolski, and yourself, other than the information contained therein?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I wasn't asked additional questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, again, the point has been made, I think, but it was the investigator that decided what questions should be asked. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will recall that my colleague and myself, in examination-in-chief, had asked you about an order that the president in fact gave to Mr. Stamboliski regarding the elimination of NLA. Do you recall those questions?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is Exhibit 1D249, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, this would be under tab 10 of your binder. And, Mr. Keskovski, this is going to be a document that I have already shown to you in examination-in-chief. It's a press report, we understand, based on the press release taken by the Security Council in relation to the events at Ljubotenski Bacila. I will ask to you look at the last paragraph in that document and it reads as follows: "At last night's meeting the council concluding that the firm action should resume to eliminate any threat to the security forces and to the citizens of the Republic of Macedonia." Is this statement, Mr. Keskovski, made by the Security Council of the Republic of Macedonia consistent with the order that you heard the president give to Mr. -- or General Stamboliski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as far as you know, do you know who is the president of the Security Council of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour this is Article 86, 1 of the constitutional of the republic; it is exhibit P91.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, do you recall being asked a number of questions by my colleague about the forthcoming signing of the Ohrid Framework Agreement. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall my colleague suggesting to you that the president was concerned, and I think you agreed, that the agreement should in fact be signed on Monday, the 13th. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you remember also the Prosecution putting to you or suggesting to you that the -- the president would be concerned on the 10th of August that further retaliatory action, I think that was the expression used, might jeopardise the signing of the agreement. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would the president also have been concerned that there should be no further NLA attack prior to the signing of the agreement on Monday?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would that concern be based on his wish, which, I think you have indicated, that the signing should take place on Monday, the 13th?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know who Mr. Vlado Buckovski is?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps could you indicate what the position of Mr. Buckovski was in the month of August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Buckovski was the minister of defence in the government of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D856.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Keskovski, I think it would be under tab 12 bis of your statement. You will see, Mr. Keskovski, this is an OTP statement taken from Minister -- in August 2001, ministry of defence, later Prime Minister Buckovski, and it's dated 11 June 2004?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask the registry to turn to page 1D00-7491.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask you, Mr. Keskovski, to locate what is paragraph 21 of that statement.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it? And I would just like to read two sentences from that statement. It says this: --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I don't see how this arises from my cross-examination, referring to the statement and also I point out that this is a statement that is not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There was extensive lengthy hourly cross-examination in relation to the reaction both of the president and of Mr. Boskoski in relation to the Karpalak incident, and the impact, if any, that this might have on the chain of events and in particular the issue of whether the Ohrid Agreement should go ahead. We believe we should be permitted to put that matter to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, that you can put, but what is the use of the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would like to test the content of the statement with the witness and whether he is able to give any indication as to the consistency of the material contained in the statement and whether he can comment upon it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Why does it arise in re-examination and why was it not used in examination-in-chief, if you see some force or relevance in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour the understanding of the Defence was that this matter was not an issue with which the Prosecution would disagree. That's the first time that they've taken issue as far as we can say with this. There had been prior occasion when we examined on this matter with other witnesses where no issue was taken with the witnesses about the chain of events and what might have led to what. This was the first time we, we understand, that this was challenged by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't think challenge is the right word. But in any event, now Mr. Apostolski has a point.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there was no translation in the Macedonian language coming to the accused, but a minute later this was resolved. This is why I stood up a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I thought you were raising on the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you better move on, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski do you recall being asked by my colleague about a number of occasions when you had been sent by the president to the terrain to provide information to him and I think you mentioned Tetovo, the Lipkovo region, and Kumanovo, and Aracinovo. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in relation to any of these particular occasion, were you the witness of the president giving orders or instructions to any of the troops that were involved in these operations?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would that include orders to the army?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would that also include, on occasions, orders to the police?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Keskovski, on a different topic, that my colleague asked you about the process of selection of your deputies within the sector of security, and I think she used the expression whether you had the last word in this matter. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think you explained and please correct me if I misstated your evidence that you took the final decision but that you would do so after consultation with the president. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. With the suggestion of the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let me ask you this then. Did you ever appoint or choose anyone to be taken in your sector of which the president disapproved of?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no such person of the security team.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And were there occasions where the president asked to you remove from your sector individuals that he disapproved of?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And just, again, moving on to a different topic, in August of 2001, do you know what telephone number Mr. Stefanovski used at the time? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall also being asked quite a number of questions by my colleague about the orders that the president gave to Mitre Despodov, and at the end of your cross-examination she put it to that you there had been no such order. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D332, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, I'll have to ask to you look at the version on your screen. It is not in the binder. It's a statement that is taken by a person whose name both my colleague and myself have mentioned to you. It's Mr. Blazo Kopacev and this is record of the statement that he gave to the Office of the Prosecutor. And I will ask the registry to please turn to page 8 of the statement and that's 1D00-3061, please. And I will ask the registry, please, to scroll down to paragraph 38. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, if I can ask you to focus on the last paragraph on that page and I will read it out to you so that you get a good translation. It says this: "Regarding the meeting between Despodov and Tarculovski on Friday, 10 August, Tarculovski asked Despodov to support his group. Despodov was reluctant. He did not want to get engaged without an order. I do not know who else from the army was present at this meeting. And then there's the passage I'm interested in, Mr. Keskovski. It says this: "I emphasise that the only source of my knowledge about the president's alleged orders to Major Despodov for action, which he allegedly received by phone from the president directly, is Major Despodov himself." Would you agree, and again, Mr. Keskovski, accepting for the sake of the argument that this is a correct -- that the information contained in it is correct, that according do the statement of Mr. Kopacev, Major Despodov in fact confirmed to him personally that he had received a direct order for action from the president on the phone. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would that be consistent with the evidence that you gave before this Chamber?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, you will be believed to know that concludes the questions that will be asked of you. The Chamber would thank you for your attendance in The Hague and the assistance you have been able to give. And you are now able to return to your normal activities. And the court officer will show you out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you allow me, since in these past several days the President Trajkovski was frequently mentioned, and yesterday was the fourth year anniversary of his death, I wish to express my condolences to his family. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, there was some matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I indicated to my colleague that I would be seeking to tender two documents that I neglected to tender during the course of evidence and I agreed to wait so that Mr. Mettraux could complete his re-examination of the witness. I wonder if I might, I know we're getting very close to the time, if I might just address, Your Honours on that matter now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: These are each opposes are they.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are these --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, they are opposed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Okay. The first of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: The first one is the personnel record that was identified by the witness as belonging to him which was 65 ter 1139 and that I -- which I referred to several documents within that record during the course of my cross-examination, and I would be seeking to tender that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Why do we need the full record?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I believe that I referred to most of the documents in that record, Your Honour. In some instances, Your Honour may have noted that some of the documents are repetitive. There's more than one document relating to the same matter but in order to provide perhaps the context of the record and the chronology of events a full record might be of assistance to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will not receive the full record, Ms. Issa. The second one.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: The second document, Your Honour, is Rule 65 ter 314.1. And that is the Article on the Ohrid framework agreement which I put to the witness regarding the events that took place, in particular in the last month leading up to the initialling of the Ohrid Agreement and then its subsequent signing. The witness had indicated that he was familiar with some of the events that I put to him, and I would submit that on that basis, that it should be received, and I'm seeking to tender it on that basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The claim doesn't see a sufficient relevance in this document either, Ms. Issa. So we will not receive it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, the hope which we expressed tentatively the other day is that it will be possible to conclude the next two witnesses in the course of the shortened session tomorrow morning. Each of them, their evidence in chief would appear to be the subject of a written statement that is received in evidence, so our hope is that the cross-examination and any re-examination in each case can be concluded in an hour. That is, an hour for each witness. Is that, Mr. Saxon, too high an ambition?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it might be too high of an ambition, but the Prosecution will endeavour to frame its cross-examinations as close to one hour as it possibly can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, we have effectively just a minute or two over an hour for each witness, because given one break, we must conclude by 11.45.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would it be acceptable to the Chamber if, for one witness the Prosecution takes a bit more than an hour and then for the second witness, of course, the Prosecution might take a bit less as long as we finish tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber will give you full flexibility within the scope of finishing by 11.45, allowing for the prospect of re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We therefore adjourn until 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 28th day of February, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.49 p.m.,
